cards.text: This song is from David, and he's talking straight to the LORD. No warm-up. No small talk. He opens with, "Vindicate me, O LORD!"

cards.question: David asks the LORD to vindicate him. What reason does David give?
David says he has trusted the LORD, but his trust has wavered.

cards.text: Then David says something I would NEVER say to anybody. When someone tastes my cookies, I'm already apologizing: it's a little dry, the oven runs hot, I was having a DAY.

cards.question: What does David ask the LORD to do to him?

answers.text: Leave him alone for a while

cards.question: David asks the LORD to examine his actions but leave his heart alone.

cards.text: Me? I'd sweat right through my apron. David? He says he's walked in God's truth, and he tells the LORD what's before his eyes.

cards.question: What does David say is before his eyes?

cards.text: Then David talks about the company he keeps. Or really, the company he DOESN'T keep, like that one coworker who slips out of the break room the second the gossip starts.

cards.question: Who does David say he does not sit with?
David says he ___ the mob of evildoers and refuses to sit with the wicked.

cards.text: Next David says, "I wash my hands in innocence". Friend, washing my hands is the first thing I do in my bakery, and honestly? It's the only step I've NEVER messed up.

cards.question: David washes his hands in innocence. What for?

answers.text: So he can go about the LORD's altar
So he can sit with the elders
So he can stand before the king

cards.question: At the LORD's altar, David plans to raise his voice in complaint.

cards.text: David wants to give thanks and tell of all God's wonderful works. Then he says what he loves, and me, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so I love ANY room with a light switch.

cards.question: David tells the LORD what he loves. What is it?

answers.text: The house where the LORD dwells
The hills where he grew up

cards.text: Then the song turns. David has a request, and it's about who he ends up with.

cards.question: What does David ask the LORD not to do?

answers.text: Take his soul away with sinners

cards.question: David describes the men of bloodshed. Their right hands are full of ___.

cards.text: Hands again, friend. David washes his in innocence, and theirs hold wicked schemes.
Then David says he WILL walk with integrity. He opened with it, he's coming back to it, and that's a man who knows his recipe.

cards.question: David says he'll walk with integrity. What does he still ask the LORD for?

answers.text: To redeem him and be merciful

cards.text: Last line of the song. David tells us where he's standing, and what he's going to do there.

cards.question: David says his feet stand on ___ ground.
David says he will bless the LORD alone, away from the congregations.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: "This song is from David, and he's talking straight to the LORD." / "No warm-up." / "No small talk." / "He opens with, 'Vindicate me, O LORD!'" The limit is three.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: "Me?" / "I'd sweat right through my apron." / "David?" / "He says he's walked in God's truth..." The limit is two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Deceitful men," describes people by their character. The wrong answers, "Tax collectors" and "Fishermen," describe people by their jobs. Because the answers aren't the same kind of thing, the right one stands out as the only moral description, and it can be picked without reasoning from the passage.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: "Next David says, 'I wash my hands in innocence'." / "Friend, washing my hands is the first thing I do in my bakery, and honestly?" / "It's the only step I've NEVER messed up." The limit is two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup on card 6 says David's request is "about who he ends up with." That rules out both wrong answers, "Hide His face from him" and "Leave him in the wilderness," because neither is about who. Only the right answer, "Take his soul away with sinners," fits the setup.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to guess a detail word in a line of poetry ("full of ___": bribes, swords or stones). Nothing earlier points to "bribes." With "men of bloodshed" in the question, "swords" looks like the reasoned pick, so the baker can only get it right by luck. This is the same pattern as the Psalm 23 bad example ("What does He anoint David's head with?").

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to guess the next word of the line ("stand on ___ ground": level, holy or dry). The setup on card 12 gives nothing to reason toward "level," so the right pick is luck.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The question says David "still" asks for redemption and mercy, which claims a connection between the two halves of the verse: he asks despite walking with integrity. Psalm 26:11 only sets the two side by side ("But I will walk with integrity; redeem me and be merciful to me").

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Two problems with "David tells us where he's standing, and what he's going to do there." First, "tells us" names who David is speaking to, and the verse doesn't say. Second, "there" places his blessing on the level ground. Psalm 26:12 says he will bless the LORD "in the congregations" and doesn't connect that to where his feet stand.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
